scope: Only the preemption aggregate-wait settlement boundary; independent candidate excludes concurrent worktree edits.

baseline_reproduction.result: Expected failure: with two blocked endpoint aborts, a subsequent cleanup deadline did not execute within one second.
baseline_reproduction.mechanism: Real runtime timer and continuation executors; mocked endpoint abort deliberately blocks on a latch. This establishes execution-boundary interference, not a production latency regression or deadlock.

implementation: The incoming BalanceContext supplies the existing serial continuation identity.
Freeze victim-resolution eligibility when aggregate waiting ends, before queuing settlement.
Run finish and dependent result callbacks on the continuation, leaving the deadline thread free of endpoint/request settlement.
Preserve ACK timing, late victim observers, exact identities and runtime producer-before-executor drain order.

added_cases: Two blocked preemption settlements do not delay another cleanup deadline.
Successful settlement respects the same-request FIFO and shutdown drains queued work.
Timeout settlement respects FIFO; a terminal arriving while queued cannot reopen incoming admission; shutdown drains work.

performance.result: All four cases passed; source manifest verified after execution.
performance.limits: This existing loopback fleet test checks general scheduling throughput and latency after warmup. It does not establish a preemption-heavy SLO, production tail-latency stability, or improvement caused by the continuation change. Warmup traffic is excluded from the reported measurements.

benchmark_audit.measurement_boundary: Planned open-loop arrival through Schedule onNext response; includes issue pacing lag. Client serialization and payload construction happen before timing. It excludes frontend fetch and real model processing.
benchmark_audit.workers: BATCH uses 750 real loopback gRPC Mock Prefill servers and 750 logical Decode endpoints. NON_BATCH uses logical role endpoints and omits frontend-to-Worker delivery. No GPU inference.
benchmark_audit.resource_model: Decode capacity is published as one billion available KV tokens and two billion total. The NON_BATCH fixture sets per-Prefill delivery inflight to 64. This is not a constrained-capacity or preemption workload.
benchmark_audit.terminal_model: BATCH accepted-batch callback immediately schedules synthetic finished-task status through real endpoint reconciliation. NON_BATCH successful route callback schedules synthetic terminal status. Simulated execution time is one millisecond; no actual inference duration is waited.
covered_correctness: Every measured response is successful and has the expected role and delivery mode.
Every measured request has exactly one response timing sample; all configured role endpoints are used.
BATCH Mock Worker receives the exact request-id set without duplicates; accepted targets match published routes.
After synthetic terminal reconciliation, active requests and P/D ledger resources and permits drain to zero.
not_covered: Real Engine execution and real WorkerStatus polling delays.
Real Decode delivery/network or transfer costs.
Cancellation, priority preemption, generation retirement, unknown RPC outcomes, and shutdown races in this traffic profile.
Stable production P99 under the production JVM/logging/monitoring/capacity configuration.
benchmark_audit.correctness_conclusion: The targeted 56 tests and 2032-test sync reactor verify specific request protocol, deadline, ordering and drain behaviors. They do not prove overall correctness for all event interleavings. The fleet benchmark alone cannot verify the preemption-timeout fix.
benchmark_audit.performance_conclusion: Only the explicit 64g ZGC + AlwaysPreTouch mock-scheduling profile passed all gates. The default-G1 control failed the BATCH 10K client-P99 gate. Overall production performance qualification remains unestablished.

default_gc_control.collector: JDK21 default G1; no ZGC, no AlwaysPreTouch and no G1 tuning flags. GC/safepoint logging enabled.
default_gc_control.other_conditions: Same source archive, host/container, 750P/750D, test method, offered rates, warmup/duration and strict gates as the ZGC profile.
default_gc_control.result: FAILED: BATCH 10000 QPS client P99 90.082ms exceeds 50ms; remaining three cases passed. Source checksums verified after execution.
default_gc_control.conclusion: The passing ZGC profile is insufficient to qualify production performance. Measured-window G1 pauses are consistent with latency sensitivity to JVM settings; one run does not isolate every contribution or establish a refactor-specific regression.

winner_fix.scope: Standalone candidate on the committed version; ongoing RequestContext and other shared worktree refactors excluded.
winner_fix.implementation: Aggregate victim-resolution completion and timeout compete to complete one CompletableFuture<Boolean>. Timeout completes false. Only the first completion supplies the immutable eligibility consumed by the existing serial continuation. No extra lifecycle field, executor, or lock-order change.

reproduction.baseline: FAILED: timeout fired before schedule returned, late victim resolution followed, yet incoming admission committed.
reproduction.fixed: PASSED: timeout result remains false, no commit, endpoint abort occurs, and the canonical late victim resolution remains available.
reproduction.method: Controlled timer invokes the real scheduled callback then completes the victim resolution before returning; real runtime continuation executes settlement. This deterministically forces the registration window, rather than relying on sleep timing.
reproduction.provenance: The shared worktree already contained this Boolean-future fix and timer regression from parallel work. This change extracts and validates that minimal fix independently.

cases: Timeout before continuation registration cannot be overridden by a late resolution.
Timeout while same-request continuation is queued cannot reopen admission.
Resolved victim followed by closed admission before settlement does not call commit and aborts the attempt.
Successful settlement follows earlier request facts; later facts follow settlement; runtime shutdown drains accepted work.
Two blocked endpoint settlements do not occupy cleanup deadline threads.

winner_fix.limits: Continuation queueing can still delay result publication and resource settlement. Timeout freezes admission eligibility, not a hard wall-clock bound on returning a result. Existing producer-before-executor shutdown ordering is retained. No claim of a preemption-heavy performance SLO or proof for every interleaving. Previously recorded default-G1 fleet P99 failure remains unresolved.
